title: How to Build an E-commerce Website That Actually Sells
excerpt: Five practical things that turn visitors into customers, from a first screen that sells to answering delivery and payment questions before checkout.
coverAlt: The LeatherCulture online store shown on a laptop and a phone
author: EireTech360 Team
body:
An online store has a few seconds to earn a visitor’s trust. Before anyone reads a product description, they have already judged the speed, the photography and how easy it looks to order. Here is what we focus on when we build an e-commerce website, and what you can check on your own store today.

1. Make the first screen do the selling

The hero should say what you sell, who it is for and what to do next, in one glance. A strong product photograph, a clear headline and a single primary button beat a slider of five competing offers every time.

2. Remove every doubt before checkout

Shoppers abandon carts when something feels uncertain. Put the answers where the questions arise:

  • Delivery: how long it takes and what it costs, shown in the announcement bar and on the product page.
  • Payment: the methods you accept, including cash on delivery where customers expect it.
  • Sizing and returns: a clear guide, and a simple way to ask before ordering.

3. Design for the phone first

Most fashion and retail traffic arrives on a phone. Buttons need to be thumb-sized, product images need to load quickly on mobile data, and the cart should never be more than one tap away.

4. Let the brand carry the price

Premium products need a premium presentation. For LeatherCulture, a Pakistani leather fashion brand, we paired editorial photography with clear collections for men, women and winter wear, so the craftsmanship is obvious before the price is.

A store that looks trustworthy and answers questions early does not need to shout about discounts.

5. Build in the basics search engines need

Crawlable collection pages, descriptive product titles, a blog and a sitemap help new customers find you without paying for every visit. These are cheapest to get right at the start of a project.

Want a store that sells?

See how we approach website development, or tell us about your project and we will suggest where to start.

title: What Actually Makes Digital Marketing Work?
excerpt: Learn how SEO, social media, paid ads and content drive growth.
coverAlt: Premium 3D EireTech360 digital marketing illustration showing SEO, social media marketing, paid advertising, content strategy and customer growth across Ireland, Europe and the USA.
author: EireTech360 Team
body:
It's easy for a company to get caught up in the hustle of marketing and not know what it's achieving. You can create Instagram posts, pay for Google clicks, and write another article for your website. However, the sales team will still ask you where the leads are coming from. It’s important that your digital marketing strategy is helping to address a need that your customers have. For most companies you will need to create the correct combination of; SEO, Social Media Marketing, Paid Advertising and Content Strategy and Creation. These all have their own unique purpose so shouldn’t be competing with each other.

SEO

Let’s say you are a commercial cleaning company based in Cork. Your website states that you provide complete solutions. However, a potential customer wants to know if you can clean offices in the evenings and how they can get a quote. This information can be difficult to find. SEO begins with understanding why there is a gap. What are people searching for? Are there dedicated pages to help answer their questions? Is your website mobile-friendly? Can Google easily find the key pages without any broken links or confusing redirects? A good SEO strategy isn’t about using keywords throughout. It’s about ensuring the correct page is helping the correct person.

Sometimes having a clear page about your services can be more beneficial than lots of generic articles. Whilst having technical improvements, logical headings and helpful links, you can’t replace real information. You should also consider local SEO. If you are providing services to specific towns or regions you will need to ensure your location information is accurate and relevant. Creating multiple pages with almost the same content but with a different city name won’t really help your customers. A good SEO strategy should help your website improve gradually. Ensuring technical issues are addressed and the information is relevant.

Social Media Marketing

Having a content calendar can help keep your team organised. However, it won’t make a dull post interesting. An architect could create a post showing how they transformed a small entrance to make the reception area accessible. A restaurant could create a post to show what changes are happening to their winter menu. A software provider could create a short video showing how they do a common task. These posts stand out as they show something real.

Social Media Marketing works best if you know who you want to target and why they would care. LinkedIn may be the right platform to use if you provide niche business services, whilst Instagram may be better if your work can be easily shown. However, they aren’t mandatory. You should ensure your posts are consistent. However, they shouldn’t be almost the same every day. You could create posts around questions your customers ask, helpful information, updates on your projects or insights from your industry. Often the best ideas come from real conversations rather than trying to keep up with the latest trends. Don’t just look at how many likes you’re getting. Are the right people asking questions or visiting your website? Social Media Marketing can be used to introduce your business to your customers however you need to ensure there is a logical flow.

Paid Advertising

Imagine clicking on an ad for a free consultation and being taken to your homepage with no mention of it. Most people won’t look through 5 menus to find it and will leave.

Whilst Paid Advertising can bring quick traffic, you are paying to get their attention. Before launching make sure you know who you are targeting, what your message is, what your landing page looks like and what you want them to do. Having a functioning mobile form may be more important than another ad. Google search ads can help target people looking for a specific service. Whereas social ads may target people who haven’t even started searching. Both can be useful depending on where they are in the buying journey. You should regularly review your Paid Advertising. Whilst you may be getting cheap clicks, if they aren’t the right people then it’s not a great deal. Ensure you are tracking useful leads and quality customers. Sometimes companies forget about the cost of finding out what works. You may need to run a new campaign with different messaging and targeting to get some useful data. If you make big changes after a disappointing day you may not have much useful information. The aim is to be careful with your spend, understand how people are reacting and make changes for a logical reason.

Content Strategy and Creation

There is a reason why the same questions keep coming up in your sales emails. People want clear answers before they spend their time and money.

A consultancy may get asked how on boarding works. A website agency may get asked the same questions about how long things take, how many revisions and what support they provide. Creating clear pages about your services or articles can make the buying process easier. Content Strategy and Creation isn’t about creating as much as possible. It’s about knowing what questions you want to answer and how. Some topics will need a quick FAQ. Whilst others will need a detailed guide, product demo or real case study. Your content should also be tailored to the stage of the customer. If they are new to your service they may need a simple explanation. If they are comparing providers they may want to know about pricing, delivery and previous work. This can help with your SEO, giving your Social Media Marketing something substantial to link to and improving your Paid Advertising pages. If your information is clear and easy to follow then having one useful page will continue to help long after your social post has been published.

Start With A Practical Strategy

Many marketing issues can occur before you even start creating ads. You want more customers but nobody has agreed on what services to focus on and who your most valuable audience is. Your marketing team may be focusing on driving traffic whilst your sales team want less but higher quality leads. Before deciding on the channels to use, it’s worth agreeing on what your goals are, what your budget is and how you will measure success.

For example, if you are a new company you may want to introduce yourself to potential customers. If you are an established service provider you may want to improve the leads coming through your website. This will influence the channels, messaging and reporting. A useful digital marketing strategy doesn’t have to be complicated. Just ensure you have clear priorities and are flexible to make changes if the data shows a better way.

Ireland, Europe & USA Aren’t One Audience

If someone searches for a Digital Marketing Agency in Ireland they may want to target customers in specific counties. You may need to ensure your examples are relevant locally, your contact information is clear and your pages are based around services people are searching for. If they are searching for a Digital Marketing Agency in the USA they may be competing with providers in individual cities/states. They may also have different expectations around pricing and searching. If they are searching for a Digital Marketing Agency in Europe it could be more complex with different languages, markets and customer behaviours. You shouldn’t use the same campaign for Dublin, Berlin and Chicago.

Local research will influence your keywords, landing pages, ad messaging and how you present your offer. If you operate in multiple countries then language isn’t the only thing to consider. Customers may react differently to pricing, descriptions and how much information they expect. Often companies looking to expand internationally will benefit from focusing on one clear market to test.

Look At The Journey

Let’s say a potential customer finds your company through a social post. A week later they read an article and then come back through a search ad to ask for a quotation.

Where should you attribute this lead to? It’s rarely the perfect answer. Look at how everything fits together. If you are getting traffic through Paid Advertising but not many leads then look at your landing page before increasing your budget. If you are getting people to visit your SEO pages but they aren’t contacting you then ensure the next step is clear. If you are getting attention through social media but it’s the wrong audience then change your topic. Your marketing reports should tell you what has happened, where your money has gone and what can be improved. EireTech360 work across all these areas for businesses in Ireland, Europe & USA. A practical digital marketing strategy will focus on what your customers are deciding, using the correct channels and measuring what is helping your business. More isn’t always better. Often you can improve the connections between what you are doing. Before spending more money find out where your best customers are currently coming from and where interested visitors are dropping off. Often this is where the most useful improvements can be made.

title: Why Your Website Gets Traffic but No Customers?
excerpt: Getting website traffic but no customers? Discover how SEO, website design and conversion rate optimisation can help turn visitors into potential customers.
coverAlt: EireTech360 blog cover showing high website traffic, increasing visitor numbers, and low customer conversions on a realistic digital analytics dashboard.
author: EireTech360 Team
body:
You may be receiving high traffic, but people aren’t taking action. Looking at your analytics (Google/Social Media/Paid Ads), you’ll notice that people aren’t getting the desired results. This can quickly become frustrating. You may not even be receiving high traffic.

Here are a few reasons why people aren’t converting,g plus ways to help improve this.

1. Wrong Traffic

Not everyone is going to be looking to purchase from your website. Many people will be researching. For example, if you’re a website development company. People searching for 'how to build a website for free’ will not want to pay an agency, whereas people searching for "professional website development services" may want to. They will be sending traffic to your website, but for different purposes.

This can be improved by using SEO. Think about what your potential customers are searching for.

  • Target certain keywords.

  • Create content to help those researching.

  • Use keywords.

  • Ensure your landing pages answer questions.

2. Poor Website

Have you ever visited a website that looked outdated and confusing? You might have bounced. Your customers will also do this. Your website doesn’t need to have lots of animations and graphics, but it needs to look professional and trustworthy. Having too many distractions, confusing navigation, outdated content, and not being mobile-friendly can cause people to bounce.

How can you improve?

  • Do you clearly understand what you offer?

  • Is your website easy to navigate on mobile?

  • Are you clear on what services you offer?

  • Are you easy to contact?

Your website needs to help your customers answer questions.

3. No Clear CTAs

People visit your website and read about your services. They love what you offer! But there are no clear CTA,s so they can’t contact you, complete an enquiry form, or know what to do. They will bounce. This is one reason why people aren’t converting from your website. Make sure you have clear CTAs.

  • Free Consultation

  • Get A Quote

  • View Our Services

  • Book An Appointment

  • Contact Our Team

Depending on what your customers are looking at on your website, make sure you have a relevant CTA. If they’re looking at an education blo,g highlight your services; if they’re looking for a quote highlight this. Make sure your CTAs are clear and concise. Avoid having too many buttons and only have one clear action.

4. Slow Website

Sometimes we overlook checking how quick your website is. Imagine visiting a page that takes a few seconds to load. You may wait a few seconds and bounce. Your customers will do this. Large images, too much scripting, too many plugins, and poor hosting can cause your website to run slowly.

This can be frustrating.

  • Make sure your images are compressed.

  • No unnecessary plugins or scripting. The website is quick on mobile.

  • Use Google PageSpeed Insights to see what you can improve.

  • Ensure your hosting is appropriate.

Whilst this won’t help you convert, it will help remove this issue.

5. Not Trustworthy

Most people won’t put their contact details/payments onto a website that doesn’t look trustworthy. Often customers want to feel assured. They will look at your reviews, past projects, service details and contact details.

If they can’t find this information they may go to a competitors site.

How can I improve trust with my customers?

  • Have real reviews.

  • Show examples of past projects.

  • Be clear on what services you offer.

  • Easy to contact.

  • Be transparent.

If you provide services to customers in Ireland, Europe & USA, make sure you show how you can provide these services and how they can work with you. Don’t overpromise and use fake testimonials. Show examples of what you can do.

6. No Relevant Landing Pages

People click on your Google ad for a free consultation but are taken to your home page. They will see lots of services. They may look around but will eventually bounce. This is because your landing pages don’t match your ads.

Ensure your landing pages match your ads. If you’re promoting SEO services, make sure they’re taken to a relevant page. If you’re promoting website development, make sure they’re taken to a page showing what services you offer and what they should do next. Ensure everything is relevant. This will help your customers decide if your service is right for them.

7. Not Analysing

Getting more traffic to your website can be encouraging, but it doesn’t show if your marketing is effective. One website could be receiving 10,000 visitors a month but only 20 enquiries, whereas another website could be receiving 2000 visitors a month but 80 enquiries. Although the second website isn’t receiving as much traffic, they are receiving more potential customers.

This is where Conversion Rate Optimisation can help. This looks at how many people are completing key actions on your website. This could be completing a form, getting a quote, or purchasing. For example, if you have 1000 visitors and 30 enquiries, your conversion rate is 3%.

Things to look at:

  • Conversion Rate – How many people are completing key actions.

  • Traffic Sources – Where are your visitors coming from?

  • Landing Pages – Which pages are generating enquiries?

  • Forms – Are people completing your forms?

  • Quality Leads – Are you receiving relevant potential customers?

Using tools like Google Analytics 4 will show you what your visitors are doing. Using Google Search Console will show you how your website is performing in Google Search. This will help identify areas to improve.

8. No Relevant SEO & Digital Marketing

Your website may look good, but you’re not seeing any rankings,s or you’re seeing good rankings but not seeing any conversions. Many companies spend lots of money on their paid ads but don’t think about how their website is. This is often because they don’t have relevant SEO, website, content & adverts. Everything should be relevant.

Using SEO will help you target potential customers. Having good content will help answer any questions. Having a good website design will help them find what they’re looking for. Using paid ads will help target those looking for specific services. Using Conversion Rate Optimisation will help improve their experience when visiting your site. EireTech36 offers website development, SEO, Digital Marketing & Technology Solutions. We help our clients improve their online presence by using an integrated approach. Understanding your audience in Ireland, Europe & the USA is key. We don’t want people to just visit our website; we want them to have an enjoyable experience.

9. How to Convert More

You don’t need to completely redesign your website or spend extra on your marketing. Often small changes can make a big difference. Look at your most popular pages. Are people quickly understanding what you offer and why? Look at the flow from visiting your page to completing an enquiry. Are your enquiry forms too long? Is your main CTA easy to find? Are your services clear? Identify one thing you can improve. Maybe simplify your form, change a confusing headline, or make your contact button easier to see on mobile. Track your results.

Not everyone will convert, and that’s okay. Just make it easy for genuinely interested customers to take action.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Why am I getting traffic but no sales?

You may not be targeting the right audience. Other reasons can be no clear CTAs, not mobile-friendly, slow loading, and not enough information on your services.

How can I improve conversions on my site?

Start by improving the pages you currently have. Make sure your services are clear, enquiry forms are simple, the website is easy to navigate on mobile & CTAs are clear. Use your analytics to see where people are bouncing.

Will SEO help me convert more?

SEO will help you target the right audience. If they can find useful information, relevant landing pages & clear next steps, they’re more likely to enquire. But it doesn’t guarantee conversions.

What’s a good conversion rate?

There is no perfect conversion rate. It depends on your industry, audience, traffic source & business goals. Just concentrate on improving your current results.

Can a website have good SEO but poor conversions?

Yes, you could have a website that is performing well in Google but not getting many enquiries.

How can I see why people are bouncing?

Look at your analytics, traffic sources, landing pages & conversion events. You can also use user testing, gather feedback from your customers & use privacy-aware behaviour analysis tools.

title: Are You Losing Time To Manual Tasks?
excerpt: Manual tasks taking up too much time? Discover how EireTech360’s workflow automation, AI tools and CRM integrations can help your business work more efficiently.
coverAlt: EireTech360 blog cover showing a stressed employee handling manual tasks alongside an AI robot automating workflows, CRM integration, customer support and data analysis to improve business efficiency.
author: EireTech360 Team
body:
There is a lot more to managing a business than just looking after your customers and providing services. You will need to reply to emails, create invoices, update spreadsheets and follow up with customers. How much time is your team spending each day doing the same tasks? Maybe they are manually inputting customer details into a spreadsheet, or someone may be creating reports or chasing approvals. Whilst these tasks may seem like small things to do, they can take up a lot of time. This is where Marketing & Business Automation and Workflow Automation can help. You can utilise technology to help you manage your information, cut down on repetition and make your day to day running more efficient.

How Much Time Are You Spending On Manual Tasks?

Many businesses have certain processes in place that everyone just accepts. Someone updates a spreadsheet each morning, someone sends out reminders for payments and your manager is creating reports on Friday afternoon. Whilst this can be an accepted part of your day to day running, it can cause issues once your business starts to grow. If you are only managing 10 customer records manually this may not be an issue but if you have hundreds of records to manage then this will become a problem. You will start to get more emails, invoices and follow ups to manage. Employees will start to spend more time on managing information than helping customers.

To see if this is happening to you: Are employees having to enter the same information? Are you missing customer queries? Do you find approvals taking longer? Are reports taking ages to create? Are departments constantly having to chase updates? If any of this sounds like it is happening to you then looking at your processes may help.

Workflow Automation

Workflow Automation can help you reduce manual tasks and complete repetitive tasks. When someone fills out the contact form on your website. Normally you would have someone look at the enquiry, add the customer details into the CRM and notify the sales team. Someone would also create an alert. With Workflow and Process Automation you can utilise compatible systems to help automate some of these tasks. Customer details can be added, the relevant member of staff notified and follow ups created.

Your team will still be managing the customer relationship but there will be less admin to do. Workflow automation can help with: Customer queries & follow ups Invoice & payment reminders Internal approvals Attendance logs Regular reports Customer onboarding You do not want to completely automate everything but you can reduce manual tasks.

CRM Integration & Setup

You may have many great tools in place but are still struggling with efficiency. Sales teams will have CRM systems, your accounts team will be managing invoicing and updating project information. Each system will be used for something. The issues start when you have to manually move information between systems. For example, if a customer sends in a query via your website. You will have to manually enter their details into the CRM, email the sales team and create a task. This can cause unnecessary work. CRM Integration & Setup can help you connect compatible systems together. Customer queries can be logged, tasks created and the relevant members of staff notified without having to re-enter information.

Before connecting your systems it is important to know what information you want to share and who should have access to it. Not all systems will be compatible with each other.

Automated Email & SMS Campaigns

Following up with customers can take up a lot of time. Some customers may want a quote, others may want to book an appointment or need a reminder. As the number of queries increases it can become difficult to manually reply to everything. Automated Email & SMS Campaigns can help with this. Customers who have booked an appointment could automatically receive a confirmation. If someone has asked for information they could receive a response letting them know when they can expect a reply.

Businesses can also provide Lead Nurturing Systems to help manage follow ups with interested customers. However you do not want to be sending unnecessary messages. Messages should still be helpful and relevant.

AI-Powered Workflow Automation

Not every issue can be solved with Artificial Intelligence. If you need to send confirmation for appointments after form completion you can normally use basic automation. However, sometimes you will have information that is not always in the same format. Say you receive hundreds of emails from customers. Some will be complaints, some will be for quotes and several will be for changing appointments. An employee may have to go through every message to see what they need to do. AI-Powered Workflow Automation can help. Depending on the system you have, AI can help with identifying what type of query it is, pulling out information, creating summaries and preparing responses. A query can be sorted and sent to the right department.

However, AI is not perfect. Any sensitive information or important decisions should still be reviewed by the correct people. Only use AI if it helps with solving the issue.

AI Chatbots & Virtual Assistants

Customers may not always be able to contact you during office hours. Someone may need information about a service late in the evening or someone may need help finding something on your website. If your team are not available they may have to wait. AI Chatbots & Virtual Assistants can help with managing basic queries. If your chatbot has been set up correctly it may be able to answer common questions, tell them about your services, gather query information or direct them to the correct information.

For example, if they need a quote they could be directed to the right enquiry form. Not everything should be automated. If they have a complex question, complaint or sensitive issue they may need personal support. Having good customer support means using the right technology to make it easy for them but also providing personal support when needed.

Custom AI Tools & Integrations

Every business will run differently. A retail business may need to improve their stock management, a service provider may be struggling with managing appointments and another company may be spending hours managing documents and customer records. Custom AI Tools & Integrations can help connect existing systems or assist with specific processes.

If a company is managing documents they could use a tool to pull out the relevant information and prepare it for review. If a business is managing multiple systems they may benefit from integrations to reduce duplicate data entry. Custom solutions can also be used with Web Application Development if they require a specific interface for their business. However, you may not need a custom solution. Compare the software you have with specific solutions. Ensure you are using the right technology to solve your issue without causing unnecessary issues.

Data Analysis & Insights

Every day you will be collecting information. Sales data, customer queries, stock records and financial reports can all provide useful information. However, this may not always be the case. Your manager may be spending hours pulling information from different departments. By the time the report is completed some of the data may have changed. Data Analysis & Insights can help you manage your information and understand how you are performing.

Automated reporting can help pull data from connected systems and create regular reports. AI can also help analyse the information to identify patterns or what needs to be looked at. A retail company could look at what products are selling well and what is out of stock. A service company could look at how quickly they are responding to queries. However, you need to ensure the data is accurate and understood. A dashboard will not help if the data behind it is not reliable.

Can Automation Help Save You Money?

Automation can help you become more efficient but it may not save you money straight away. You will have to pay for the software, set up, maintenance and training. Say an employee is spending 30 minutes each working day creating the same report. Over 5 days this will be 2.5 hours. If the report can be automated this time can be spent doing other things.

However, you need to consider: How long is the task taking? How often are mistakes made? How much will automation cost? Will employees need training? How will customers benefit? Automation can also cause issues if not set up correctly. If the workflow isn’t set up correctly incorrect information may be sent repeatedly or records may not be updated correctly. Always test and monitor.

How EireTech360 Can Help You Run A Smarter Business

Every business will have different issues they face. A retail business may need help with managing their stock, a service provider may be struggling with customer follow ups and another company may be spending hours creating reports. At EireTech360 we can help you improve your operations with Marketing & Business Automation, Workflow Automation, Custom AI Development and connected solutions. We can help with: CRM Integration & Setup AI Chatbots & Virtual Assistants AI-Powered Workflow Automation Custom AI Tools & Integrations Data Analysis & Insights We like to understand how your processes are currently running and identify where technology can help make everyday tasks easier.

We work with businesses across Ireland, Europe and the USA and look at what their operational needs are and what systems they have. Our goal is to reduce manual tasks, make information easier to manage and give employees more time to focus on their roles.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Marketing & Business Automation?

Marketing & Business Automation is using technology to help automate repetitive marketing and business tasks. This includes customer follow ups, updating information and regular communications.

What is AI-Powered Workflow Automation?

Using AI to help with your workflows. This can include sorting emails, pulling out information and creating summaries. Some tasks can still be done using basic automation rules.

Can AI Chatbots & Virtual Assistants replace customer support?

They can help with answering basic questions and managing queries but complex situations may still need personal support.

Are Custom AI Tools & Integrations suitable for small businesses?

Yes depending on what your business needs and budget. Smaller companies should look at whether they can use existing software.

How can automation help improve efficiency?

It can reduce duplication, help manage follow ups, connect compatible systems and make reporting easier.

Will it work with my existing software?

Many business systems offer integrations however not all will be compatible. Look at your existing systems and what connections you have.

Is it expensive?

It depends on the software, integrations and complexity of your workflow. Simple processes may be affordable but more customised systems can be costly.

Final Thoughts

Manual tasks will always be a part of running a business. Not every task will need AI and not every decision should be automated. However, if your employees are having to repeatedly enter information, create the same reports or chase approvals then it is worth looking at how you are doing this. Start off by looking at one task that is causing unnecessary delays. Can Workflow Automation, CRM Integration or the right AI solution help improve this? You do not need to change everything. Sometimes just improving one task that you do everyday can make a noticeable difference.

Growing your business shouldn’t mean more repetitive tasks for your team.

title: Why Do People Uninstall Apps?
excerpt: Why do people uninstall apps? Explore common issues with slow loading, confusing navigation, sign-ups and trust, and how better UI/UX design can help users stay.
coverAlt: EireTech360 blog cover showing a mobile app user considering uninstalling an application due to slow loading, confusing navigation, excessive notifications and difficult sign-up, highlighting common mobile app user experience problems.
author: EireTech360 Team
body:
You downloaded the app because it made things easier for you. However, when setting up your account and using the app, there might be issues. It may take too long to load or be confusing.

Things To Consider

You want people to download your app and enjoy using it. A great app means you can do everything you want without any issues.

Why Would They Uninstall?

Bad First Impressions

Did your last app have a good first impression? Was it confusing and took time to figure out? First impressions are really important, and your app has no loyalty. If it is confusing and takes too long to load, you may lose users.

UI/UX Design

UI Design – Buttons, Screens, Menus & Layout. UX Design – Easy to use.

Improvements

Easy Home Screen. Main Features Easy to find. Easy to Navigate. No extra pop-ups. Easy to Understand What The App Does. Easy to Understand.

Too Much Information

Say you download a food delivery app to help you when you’re hungry. However, you need to create an account, confirm your email, enter your personal details, and opt in to notifications. Before you get to see the menu? Do you continue? Some may, but some may give up. Too much information can cause issues.

Not every app will require information. A shopping app may allow customers to browse before they need to create an account. Booking apps may let visitors browse services. Some apps may require secure logins. Only ask for what you need. Try to gain trust from your users.

Slow Performance

No one likes to wait for apps to load. Say you wanted to see your appointment details, but the screen takes a few seconds to load. When clicking on your booking, you are taken to a new screen. Eventually you give up. Even if you have a great-looking app, it can cause frustration if it is taking too long to load. Having a fast app can help you gain a better impression from your users. During your iOS & Android App Development, you should think about how fast your app is. Large files, bad coding, and extra processes can cause slow performance.

Improvements

Optimize your images & large files. Test main features on different devices. No extra information. Test for crashes & issues. Test on slow internet. Your app should perform well.

Information Not Easy to Find

Your app may have great features, but are they easy to find? Maybe your banking app makes it difficult to see your balance, or your shopping app has a hard-to-find checkout button. This can cause frustration. A great Mobile App User Experience will help your users complete tasks.

Your interface should be easy to understand so you know: Where you are. What you can do. What will happen when you click on something. A fitness app may have your daily activity and training plan on your home screen. Booking apps should be easy to book. Your design should help your users. Sometimes less is more.

No Solution

A lot of businesses get excited about creating an app. They imagine it will have great features, custom dashboards, and complex integrations. But why would they need this? If there are no extra features or useful tools and it has the same information as your website, then they wouldn’t want to use it. Your app should have a clear solution. A restaurant app could help users order and track deliveries. An Employee Management app could help you manage employee attendance, holiday requests, and daily tasks. A retail app could help users track their orders.

Businesses can create tools for browsers using Web Application Development. Choose the right option. Don’t get too excited and know what issues you are trying to solve.

Too Many Notifications

Notifications can be useful. They can help remind you of your appointment, when your delivery will be, and keep you updated. However, if you are getting too many promotional messages throughout the day, you may switch off notifications or uninstall the app. Notifications should have a purpose. Having reminders for your appointment, security alerts, and order updates can be really useful. However, too many promotional messages can cause frustration.

Considerations

Relevant. No duplicates. Personalised. Short. Respect their privacy. To keep them updated.

Not Trustworthy

Users will be cautious about putting personal information into an app. If your app is asking for payment or device information, they will want to know why. Would you trust your calculator if it asked for access to your contacts and location?

Apps that are asking for payment or personal information should be trustworthy. Having a professional-looking app will help increase trust. Consider: Secure Logins. Proper Data Security. Have a reason for asking for their information. Don’t ask for unnecessary permissions. If you do ask for permissions, make sure there is a reason. Users should know how their information is being used.

No Testing

A developer may spend months creating an app. It has a great design, features, and the development team knows exactly what is on each screen. However, someone who doesn’t know the app well may struggle. Maybe the buttons are unclear, instructions are confusing, or there is too much information to sign up. Testing your app can help. During your UI/UX Design For Apps, you can use interactive prototyping and usability testing to help spot any issues. Ask someone to complete a realistic task without explanation. Can they book an appointment? Where are they struggling? Can they easily navigate through the app? Can they book?

This can help spot any issues. The aim is not to prove your app works, but you will be able to see areas to improve.

Thinking You Are Done

Launching an app is an amazing achievement. However, there are other factors to consider. Operating systems can change, customer expectations can change, and there can be unexpected bugs. App Maintenance & Updates are important. Regular maintenance will help you spot any technical issues and improve current features.

Considerations

Crash / Technical issues. Customer Feedback / Complaints. Device compatibility. Hard-to-use features. Performance / Security issues. Don’t add extra features just because people want more. Sometimes improving current issues will improve the experience. Your app should continue to develop to meet the needs of your users.

How Will You Know Why They Are Leaving?

If your app isn’t being used much, you won’t know why. You need to know why. Are they leaving when signing up? Are they leaving a particular screen? Are they unable to complete key tasks due to technical issues? Using App Analytics, usability testing & customer feedback can help. You can also monitor App User Retention. This will show how many people are coming back after a certain amount of time.

This will depend on what your app does. A travel booking app may not be used as much as an employee attendance app, which may be used daily. Don’t try to retain a certain number of users. Try to ensure your users are completing the tasks your app was created for.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Why Do People Uninstall Apps?

Common reasons people uninstall apps are because they are too slow to load, confusing to use, difficult to sign up, have too many notifications, and don’t meet expectations. Some may uninstall as they no longer need it.

How Can I Improve My Mobile App User Retention?

Improve performance, make it easy to sign up, fix any technical issues, and ensure key features are easy to find. Monitor customer feedback and regularly test improvements.

Does UI/UX Design Affect App Retention?

Yes. Having easy to navigate & easy to use features will make your app easy to use. If it is badly designed, users may become frustrated.

What Is The Difference Between UI & UX Design?

UI design is the visual part of your app. This could be buttons, layouts & menus. UX design is the overall experience.

Should I Create an iOS App, Android App, or Both?

This will depend on your audience, budget & features. Research your target audience to see if you want to go native or cross-platform.

Why Is App Maintenance Important?

Apps should be updated to ensure they are compatible, secure & reliable. This could include fixing bugs, reviewing performance, and improving based on user feedback.

Can I Replace A Mobile App With A Web App?

Sometimes. Web apps can provide tools for your business. However, if your app requires specific device features, you may want to go native.
